title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §1 'Connexions sur torseurs affines' (affine torsors). Setup from the previous page: S/T is a relative scheme and E is a locally free O_S-module. The first principal-parts sequence 0 → E⊗Ω¹_{S/T} → P¹_{S/T}(E) → E → 0 has a canonical splitting d¹_E : E → P¹(E). This splitting is q^{-1}O_T-linear but not O_S-linear. It lets one write every section of P¹(E) uniquely as d¹_E x + ω. From this one gets the twisting rule (4): f(d¹_E x + ω) = d¹_E(fx) + (fω − x⊗df).

A connection is an O_S-linear splitting δ_E of the sequence. Any additive splitting can be written δx = d¹_E x − d⁰_E x for some additive map d⁰_E : E → E⊗Ω¹. On this page Grothendieck works out when δ is O_S-linear. Requiring fδx = δ(fx) and using (4) gives d¹(fx) − f d⁰x − x⊗df = d¹(fx) − d⁰(fx). This is equivalent to the Leibniz rule (7): d⁰(fx) = f d⁰x + x⊗df. Written with the right Ω^•-module structure, it becomes (7'): d⁰(xf) = d⁰(x)f + x df. He remarks (NB) that d⁰_E satisfying (7) is what is usually called a connection.

He then states the standard facts. d⁰_E extends uniquely to a degree-1 additive endomorphism d^•_E of E⊗Ω^•_{S/T} satisfying the graded Leibniz rule (9): d(φω) = d(φ)ω + (−1)^{deg φ} φ dω. One has d^•∘d^• = 0 if and only if the composite d¹_E d⁰_E : E → E⊗Ω² vanishes. That composite is O_S-linear; viewed as a section of Hom(E, E⊗Ω²) it is the curvature tensor. The connection is integrable when the curvature vanishes, i.e. when E⊗Ω^• is a complex.

The next page goes on to define de Rham cohomology with coefficients as hypercohomology, the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence, and functoriality and pullbacks. These are preparatory foundations for the Gauss–Manin connection.
errors: The text says 'compte tenu de (5)'. The computation actually uses formula (4) from the previous page, the twisting rule for f·d¹_E x. In the manuscript the reference is probably '(4,' (Grothendieck writes ',' for ')'), so this looks like a transcription slip.
No mathematical errors. The signs in (7), (7') and (9) are consistent with the right-module convention he adopts.

ideas.what: Connection as an O_S-linear splitting of the first principal-parts (jet) sequence, equivalently a Leibniz-rule map d⁰_E : E → E⊗Ω¹
ideas.modern_name: Connection via 1-jets / Atiyah-type splitting; equivalence with the Koszul connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Atiyah (1957) for the jet/Atiyah-sequence viewpoint; Grothendieck (Crystals, 1968), Katz, Deligne (LNM 163, 1970) in algebraic geometry
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); EGA IV §16 for principal parts

ideas.what: Unique extension of a connection to a degree-1 derivation on E⊗Ω^• (graded Leibniz rule)
ideas.modern_name: Extended covariant derivative / de Rham complex with coefficients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Koszul, Cartan); algebraic version in Katz and Deligne LNM 163

ideas.what: Curvature as the O_S-linear composite d¹∘d⁰; integrability iff d²=0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Katz 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970), Deligne LNM 163

deep.surprise_reason: These are textbook foundations on connections, curvature and the de Rham complex with coefficients. They appear in Grothendieck's own Crystals paper, in Katz and in Deligne. The only distinctive touch is deriving the Leibniz rule from the splitting of P¹(E) using the 'affine torsor' language, which is standard too.
transcription_corrections: 'compte tenu de (5)' should probably read 'compte tenu de (4)', i.e. (4) with the closing parenthesis written as a comma.
The NB line reads roughly 'On dit souvent que d⁰_E (5) satisfaisant (7) est une connexion sur E rel. à T'. The crossed-out line beneath it begins 'On sait alors qu'il…'.
The strike-through in the line '[-une dérivation antidérivation-]' appears to be 'une dérivation ou antidérivation'.
The end of the line 'qui [-...-], satisfasse : la relation suivante' continues on the next line as 'rel. à la structure de Ω^•_{S/T}-module à droite'.
